assumptions: Polish transposition creates recurring portfolio-level decisions rather than only one-off installer-led compliance checks.
Commercial owners will pay separately for vendor-neutral orchestration.
Qualified auditors and engineers can be subcontracted while maintaining acceptable margins and quality.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: One paid multi-site portfolio assessment proving an identifiable budget owner, sales-cycle length, quantified avoided cost or delay, and a repeatable margin after all engineering and acquisition costs.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Portfolio owners may need a vendor-neutral layer translating phased solar rules and fragmented site data into comparable capex decisions and evidence.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Delays and engineering rework can be costly, but Polish implementation, triggering frequency, budget ownership, and willingness to unbundle orchestration are unknown.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: High-ticket assessments can fund delivery, though subcontracted engineering, long sales cycles, payment delays, liability, and project-heavy work constrain operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Multi-site commercial portfolios are coherent and valuable, but suitability exemptions and uncertain national implementation narrow the reachable near-term market.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor neutrality and portfolio comparability differentiate the offer, yet engineering firms and installers can bundle screening to win implementation work.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning portfolio workflows could lead to monitoring, tender intelligence, retrofit planning, evidence management, and adjacent building compliance.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Rule mappings, benchmark costs, and site outcomes can accumulate, but customer access is unsigned and specialist partners or incumbents can reproduce the service.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Cross-installer comparability and an audit trail could improve portfolio decisions, but quantified savings over bundled adviser offerings are absent.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Phased EU building requirements create a credible future demand wave, although timing and enforcement in Poland remain uncertain.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct enterprise outreach and referrals are plausible but no property relationship is controlled, and long sales cycles conflict with part-time launch constraints.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Analytics can be automated and engineering subcontracted, but qualified specialists, liability, building data, procurement, and 15-25 weekly hours remain demanding.

highest_value_structural_change: Embed the workflow under a multi-year portfolio agreement that covers annual capex planning and evidence updates, rather than selling standalone assessments.
main_structural_strength: Regulatory complexity and fragmented site procurement create a potentially valuable portfolio-level coordination position with high contract values.
primary_score_limiter: Demand is future-weighted and the company has no controlled buyer relationship, validated price, or protection from installer and engineering-firm bundling.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Suitability and feasibility exceptions reduce mandatory volume, while installers may provide assessments cheaply as part of winning installation work.
